events.description: Riot at the US Capitol, which delayed the episode by a week
Pompeo delivers a speech on the Iran-al-Qaeda axis, and State Department Rewards for Justice announces details on al-Qaeda leaders in Iran
actors: US State Department Rewards for Justice

events.description: Last-minute Trump-administration designations, including the Houthis and the head of Iraq's Popular Mobilization Forces
Abu Muhammad al-Masri, al-Qaeda deputy emir, killed in Iran by Israelis at US behest; first reported on al-Qaeda channels and then confirmed by the New York Times and, in this speech, by Pompeo
US embassy bombings in East Africa, for which al-Masri is wanted
Atiyah Abd al-Rahman killed
Abdelmalek Droukdel killed in Mali
Hamza bin Laden reportedly killed in Karam, a Haqqani stronghold
Pompeo delivers a speech on the Iran-al-Qaeda axis, saying al-Qaeda has a new home base in Iran and fewer al-Qaeda operatives are in Afghanistan than in decades.
Treasury response to the DoD IG says al-Qaeda is gaining strength in Afghanistan under Taliban protection, with a joint Haqqani-al-Qaeda unit, and that the Taliban and al-Qaeda meet regularly.
actors: Department of Defense Office of Inspector General

events.description: US-Taliban deal; Treasury says the Taliban and al-Qaeda kept a strong relationship in the months after it.
Treasury assessment, as of May 2020, that the Taliban and al-Qaeda maintain a strong relationship and meet regularly.
Husam Abd al-Rauf ('Hassam al-Dharouf'), a senior al-Qaeda management figure, killed in Afghanistan.
US Embassy bombings in Kenya and Tanzania, carried out by al-Qaeda operatives who per the 9/11 Commission received tactical expertise from Iran and Hezbollah.
9/11 Commission report is released, finding links between Iran and al-Qaeda; the press initially reported it, then ignored it.
Bin Laden letter to Abu Hamza al-Muhajir calling Iran the main artery for funds, personnel and communication, later released by ODNI.
actors: Office of the Director of the National Intelligence

events.description: Series of Obama-era Treasury and State designations of al-Qaeda operatives in Iran, spelling out the secret agreement and the 'core pipeline'.
Designation of Iran's Ministry of Intelligence and Security for facilitating al-Qaeda, including passports.
actors: Iranian Ministry of Intelligence and Security

events.description: Designation detailing the terms of the Iran-al-Qaeda agreement and reshuffling of the network in Iran.
Roggio and Joscelyn debate Peter Bergen at the New America Foundation about al-Qaeda's supposed defeat.
US troop level in Afghanistan falls to about 2,500.
Reuters retitles its piece to 'Pompeo says Iran gives al-Qaeda new home base. Analysts skeptical' and adds the Iranian government denial.
Yasin al-Suri said to have been operating in Iran since 2005 under an agreement with the regime.
Files recovered at bin Laden's compound, including Suri's personnel file.
US Treasury designated Yasin al-Suri's al-Qaeda facilitation network in Iran, exposing the secret Iran-al-Qaeda deal.
Atiyah Abd al-Rahman killed (hosts also say mid-2011).
Five senior al-Qaeda leaders, including Abu Muhammad al-Masri and Saif al-Adel, freed by Iran after al-Qaeda kidnapped an Iranian diplomat; three went to Syria and were killed.
Abu Muhammad al-Masri killed in Iran.

Pompeo speech on the Iran-al-Qaeda axis, claiming Iran allowed al-Qaeda a new operational headquarters after a 2015 change; accompanied by new designations of four al-Qaeda figures including Maghrebi and Sultan Yusuf Hassan al-Arif.
CIA assessment sent to the State Department in the past week, reportedly concluding that Masri and Saif al-Adel reorganized al-Qaeda's global management from Iran after 2015.
Abu Muhammad al-Masri killed in Iran; first reported by the New York Times (referenced as an example).
Pompeo's speech on the Iran–al-Qaeda axis; hosts criticize the press dismissal of it.

key_claims: Pompeo's speech does not signal a push for war with Iran; he himself said the military option against al-Qaeda in Iran is riskier than it was in Afghanistan.
Abu Muhammad al-Masri, al-Qaeda's deputy emir, was killed in Iran on 7 Aug 2020 by Israelis at US behest, a targeted killing rather than a regime-change conflict.
Senior al-Qaeda leaders Saif al-Adel and Abdul Rahman al-Maghrebi (Zawahiri's son-in-law and general manager) are in Iran, so about three of the top four leaders have been in Iran.
Al-Qaeda leadership is distributed across affiliates (AQIM, AQAP, Syria, al-Shabaab), so Iran is not the only home base.
Zawahiri is probably in Pakistan/Afghanistan, likely protected by the Haqqani Network in its strongholds.
Pompeo's comparison to Afghanistan is flawed because al-Qaeda was in cities such as Kabul and Kandahar in 2001, not just remote mountains.
The hosts say the 2001 AUMF has been stretched beyond its limits and that any war with Iran would need new congressional authorization.
Al-Qaeda management is geographically dispersed (Iran, Yemen, Syria, Somalia, Afghanistan, Pakistan), and the US government has not given a real assessment of its structure.
Al-Qaeda is likely to shift more leaders into Afghanistan and Pakistan as the US leaves, reducing its dependence on the IRGC.
Treasury's Jan 2021 assessment says al-Qaeda is gaining strength in Afghanistan under Taliban protection, with embedded mentors and a joint Haqqani-al-Qaeda unit.
The Taliban-al-Qaeda relationship is strong and symbiotic, with regular meetings continuing after the Feb 29, 2020 US-Taliban deal.
Pompeo's statements are inconsistent: he calls al-Qaeda a shadow of its former self when defending the Taliban deal, but says it is poised to gain strength in Iran.
The Iran-al-Qaeda facilitation network is not clandestine but based on an agreement with the Iranian regime, as shown in bipartisan US designations from 2011 to 2016 and the 9/11 Commission.
Bin Laden's 2007 letter calling Iran the 'main artery' parallels the Obama-era 'core pipeline' language.
The hosts say US estimates of 50-100 al-Qaeda members in Afghanistan (2010-2016) versus about 200 now contradict Pompeo's claim of fewer operatives than in decades.
The Iran-al-Qaeda relationship is a long-standing alliance or working arrangement of convenience dating to the 1990s, not a new development.
A July 2011 Treasury designation showed Yasin al-Suri's facilitation network operated in Iran under an explicit agreement with the regime, negotiated by Atiyah Abd al-Rahman.
The 2011 Obama-era designations make this a bipartisan factual case that Pompeo failed to cite and the press ignored.
Al-Qaeda's senior leadership in Iran (Masri, Saif al-Adel, Maghrebi, Suri) plausibly constitutes an operational headquarters, lending some credence to Pompeo's wording, though 'new' is questionable.

Pompeo downplays Afghanistan; one newly designated figure, Sultan Yusuf Hassan al-Arif, is a key al-Qaeda operative in Afghanistan and Iran, which suggests al-Qaeda in Iran helps direct operations in support of the Taliban.
The relationship is complex: al-Qaeda and Iran are also enemies at times (Syria, Yemen, kidnappings, detentions), but cooperate strategically.
A CIA assessment reportedly concluded that Masri and Saif al-Adel reorganized al-Qaeda's global management structure from Iran after 2015, but the CIA gave no official public assessment.
The hosts argue that the press gives credence to anonymous intelligence officials while dismissing Pompeo's on-the-record claims about al-Qaeda and Iran.
They say there are well-documented facts on al-Qaeda in Iran, such as designations and the killing of Abu Muhammad al-Masri, that the press ignores.
The hosts say Congress should provide proper oversight of the intelligence and the legal basis for action but often engages in political posturing.
The hosts say they are not calling for war with Iran but want the facts reported accurately.
